title: Add types with JSDoc
when: The user wants type safety or editor hints in plain JavaScript without a compile step.
prompt:
Goal: Plain JavaScript with JSDoc types on every public function and shared data shape, checkable by an editor with // @ts-check.
Steps:
1. Define shared shapes once with @typedef {Object} Invoice and @property lines, or in a types.js file imported with @typedef {import("./types.js").Invoice}.
2. Annotate each exported function: @param {string} id, @param {{ limit?: number }} [opts], @returns {Promise<Invoice[]>}.
3. Use unions for known values: @param {"draft" | "sent" | "paid"} status.
4. Type callbacks and events: @param {(item: Invoice) => boolean} predicate, @param {MouseEvent} event.
5. Add // @ts-check at the top of each file and fix the mismatches it reveals in the code, not by widening to any.
6. Mark nullable returns explicitly (Invoice | null) and handle them at call sites.
Quality bar:
- No {*} or {any} unless the value really is unknown.
- Typedefs live in one place.
- Comments describe meaning, types describe shape.
Pitfalls:
- Types that disagree with what the code returns.
- Copying the same object shape in many files.
- Casting away errors instead of fixing the code.
Verify:
- [ ] Every export has @param and @returns.
- [ ] Typedef names match their use.
- [ ] Nullable values are handled.
- [ ] Files parse.
Output: Annotated source files and types.js for shared typedefs.

examples.input: add types to cart.js without a build step
examples.output: @typedef CartItem, typed addItem and total, // @ts-check found a string price bug
